ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
On a smooth horizontal surface, two objects A and B are placed side by side, with $\mathrm{m_A} = 5\mathrm{kg}$ and $\mathrm{m_B} = 3\mathrm{kg}$. A horizontal external force $\mathrm{F} = 16\mathrm{N}$ is applied to push the two objects, causing them to move together in uniformly accelerated linear motion.

1. Find the magnitude of the elastic force between A and B.

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: On a smooth horizontal surface, two objects A and B are placed side by side, with $\mathrm{m_A}=5\mathrm{kg}$ and $\mathrm{m_B}=3\mathrm{kg}$. A horizontal external force $\mathrm{F}=16\mathrm{N}$ is applied to push the two objects, causing them to move together in uniformly accelerated linear motion. Find the magnitude of the elastic force between A and B.
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, there are two blocks in contact with each other placed on a horizontal surface indicated by diagonal lines; the block on the left is labeled A, and the block on the right is labeled B; a horizontal external force F acts on A from the left side, with the arrow pointing to the right, so A pushes B to move to the right together. The horizontal surface is smooth, so friction is not considered. Reasoning: Treat A and B as a whole; the only external force in the horizontal direction is F=16 N, and the total mass is m_A+m_B=5 kg+3 kg=8 kg, so the common acceleration is a=F/(m_A+m_B)=16/8=2 m/s^2. Then analyze B separately; in the horizontal direction, B is only acted on by the contact elastic force exerted on it by A, and this elastic force provides B's acceleration, therefore N=m_B a=3×2=6 N.
